Ostar · Makkakah

Troubleshooting and practical guidance

Jerry Pop · Reinterpretable Kerot studio

A working browser K0 interpreter with explicit simulated driver attachments. The app can assemble, step, and execute the final quilt or your own primitive source. No physical device, shell, network, or external account is accessed.

Complete primitive program library

Load any supplied Kerot example, or select one of the eight quilt modes below. Edit the source and input, then assemble or record a revision. All executions use the declared K0 host.

Templates and atemples

Load a reusable source template, then edit an atemple variant. Loading replaces editor text, input, and attachments; export work you want to keep first. Nothing executes automatically.

Source and input

Edited source can be reinterpreted with captured inputs and drivers. Use Assemble to start a new session with changed inputs or attachments. New live input is added only by the feed control below.

Archangel attachable port system

Core ports 0 output, 1 input, and 2 stop are fixed. Choose optional simulated drivers for the next assembled machine.

Archangel here describes explicit, reviewable attachment permissions. It supplies no spiritual or hardware authority.

Reinterpretable programming

Edit source and reinterpret it with the active revision's original input and attachments. Each reinterpretation starts fresh memory and devices. Later fed input is not captured.

Up to ten revisions and two million source characters remain in this page. Export to retain them across reloads. Assemble starts a new session; recording edited source, input, and drivers preserves history. Reinterpretation contract.

Import validates every source revision, byte input, and driver selection before replacing the session. Replay and import create fresh machines.

Machine and drivers
No background execution: another run click continues a budget-limited machine. Waiting requires input or a queued byte; halted/faulted machines require a fresh assembly, reinterpretation, or replay.
